diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The baseline agent correctly identified and fixed the primary build failure (ModuleNotFoundError for langchain_core by wrapping the import in try/except), but a secondary pre-existing test failure (test_record_timestamp with timestamp equality) was dismissed as 'out of scope'. The verifier runs the full test suite via run_passed.sh, so this timing-related test failure causes the overall build to fail. The agent needs guidance to recognize that ALL failing tests must be addressed when the verifier is a full build/test script, not just the obvious import error. The timestamp issue stems from millisecond-precision truncation in helpers.py where sleep(0.15) can still produce identical millisecond timestamps on fast systems. The analyze-ci skill is most relevant as it would help diagnose the full set of CI failures rather than stopping at the first fix.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The skill guides analyzing failed CI jobs but does not emphasize that in build-repair tasks, agents must address ALL failing tests reported by the build script, not just the primary/obvious error. The agent fixed the import error and dismissed a secondary timestamp test failure as 'out of scope', but that failure caused the overall build verifier to fail.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add explicit guidance that when analyzing CI failures for build-repair tasks: (1) enumerate every failing test/job, not just the first or most obvious one; (2) do not label secondary failures as 'pre-existing' or 'out of scope' unless the verifier explicitly excludes them — the verifier typically runs the full test suite and any failure causes the build to fail; (3) for timing/timestamp-related test failures (e.g., assertions that two timestamps differ after a sleep), investigate precision issues in time helpers (millisecond truncation, timezone-naive datetime) and consider increasing precision or sleep duration.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The skill covers writing effective tests but does not address diagnosing flaky timestamp/timing tests where millisecond-precision truncation causes identical timestamps despite a sleep. The baseline failure shows two timestamps equal to '2026-09-20T02:11:16.942Z' after a 0.15s sleep, indicating the underlying helper function in helpers.py uses millisecond precision which can collide.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add a section on diagnosing and repairing timing-sensitive tests: when timestamp equality/inequality assertions fail intermittently or on fast systems, inspect the timestamp helper for precision loss (e.g., isoformat(timespec='milliseconds')) and either (a) increase precision to microseconds, (b) use monotonic counters, or (c) widen the sleep interval. Note that fixing the production helper (helpers.py) may be the correct build repair rather than modifying the test.
